B1-g0-C1.title: Leave-one-out empirical-CDF normalisation for inductive MVFA scoring
B1-g0-C1.summary: Replace test-set min-max with each branch's (and level's) leave-one-out empirical CDF over support-normal patch scores; keep the 0.5 fusion and max pooling.
B1-g0-C1.research_idea: Independent variable: normaliser (test-set min-max; support percentiles as in the problem; support LOO empirical CDF). Reference set R_bl: patch scores of each support computed against a memory bank of the other K-1 supports (few-shot) or the text anchors (zero-shot). F_bl(s) = (rank of s in R_bl + 0.5)/(|R_bl| + 1); fused map = 0.5 F_zero + 0.5 F_few (averaged over levels as in MVFA); image score = max of fused map. Dependent variables: image/pixel AUROC; sensitivity at 95% specificity with tau = 95th percentile of LOO support image scores; realised specificity; per-image score shift under test-set resampling (exactly zero by construction for inductive variants).
B1-g0-C1.hypothesis: At K >= 4, LOO empirical-CDF normalisation keeps image and pixel AUROC within 1 point of the transductive pipeline, and its support-derived threshold gives realised specificity within 5 points of 95% on every held-out dataset, with a smaller miss than the percentile normaliser at K = 2.
B1-g0-C1.rationale: Percentiles use two points of the support distribution and are noisy for small K. Following ReCAP's non-parametric normal memory, each branch can instead be mapped through the full leave-one-out empirical CDF of support-normal patch scores, which places both branches on the same [0, 1] scale defined only by the K supports, before MVFA's unchanged 0.5 fusion and max pooling.
B1-g0-C1.method: 1) test_few.py: refactor into score_image(x, model, support_feats, refs) that uses no other test image; remove the test-set min-max block. 2) utils.py: build_refs(support_feats, text_feats): for i in 1..K, few-shot patch scores of support i against the bank of the others and zero-shot scores; store sorted arrays per branch and level. 3) cdf(s, R) via torch.searchsorted. 4) Fusion 0.5/0.5 and max pooling unchanged. Hyper-parameters: none beyond nominal specificity 95%; no training.
B1-g0-C1.experiment: Protocol: leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA checkpoints retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2, 4, 8, 16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws, mean and std; fusion weight 0.5 and max pooling unchanged in every variant. Baselines: the original transductive pipeline (test-set min-max) and the percentile normaliser of the problem statement (1st/99th percentiles of leave-one-out support patch scores). Motivating measurement for all variants: AUROC spread of the transductive pipeline over random half-size test subsets and at 10% and 50% prevalence. Metrics: image/pixel AUROC, sensitivity at 95% specificity, realised specificity, ECE after a logistic map fitted on source validation. Falsified if AUROC drops by more than 1 point at K >= 4.
provenance: MadCLIP: Few-shot Medical Anomaly Detection with CLIP
Beyond Static Anchors: Bounded Prototype Conditioning for Language-Free Medical Anomaly Detection

B1-g0-C2.title: Source-episode scale with support re-centring for inductive MVFA scoring
B1-g0-C2.summary: Learn each branch's scale on simulated few-shot episodes from the source modalities and set only its location from the K target supports, replacing test-set min-max.
B1-g0-C2.research_idea: Independent variable: normaliser (test-set min-max; support percentiles; source-episode scale + support location). On each source modality's validation split, 50 episodes of K normal supports and 40 queries; for branch b, z_b = (s_b - mu_supp,b) / sigma_b, where mu_supp,b is the median LOO support patch score of the episode and sigma_b is fitted across episodes as the median absolute deviation of normal query patch scores around mu_supp,b. On the target only mu_supp,b is computed. Dependent variables: image/pixel AUROC, sensitivity at 95% specificity, realised specificity, per-image score shift.
B1-g0-C2.hypothesis: At K = 2, the source-episode scale with support re-centring loses at least 1 AUROC point less than the support-percentile normaliser relative to the transductive pipeline, and at K >= 4 both are within 1 point of it.
B1-g0-C2.rationale: Support statistics from K normal images are noisy for small K. MVFA is trained on five source modalities with validation splits, so the SCALE of each branch can be learned there from simulated few-shot episodes and transferred, while only the LOCATION is set on the target from its K supports. This keeps the 0.5 fusion and max pooling and separates a stable learned scale from a cheap per-modality shift.
B1-g0-C2.method: 1) calibrate_episodes.py: for each training fold, sample episodes on source validation splits using the trained model's scoring functions; estimate sigma_b per branch and level; save calib.json. 2) test_few.py: per-image z_b with mu from the target supports (LOO) and sigma from calib.json; then the unchanged 0.5 fusion and max pooling; test-set min-max removed. Hyper-parameters: 50 episodes, 40 queries, K matched to the target K; no adapter training.
B1-g0-C2.experiment: Protocol: leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA checkpoints retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2, 4, 8, 16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws, mean and std; fusion weight 0.5 and max pooling unchanged in every variant. Baselines: the original transductive pipeline (test-set min-max) and the percentile normaliser of the problem statement (1st/99th percentiles of leave-one-out support patch scores). Motivating measurement for all variants: AUROC spread of the transductive pipeline over random half-size test subsets and at 10% and 50% prevalence. Metrics: image/pixel AUROC, sensitivity at 95% specificity, realised specificity, score shift. Falsified if the source-episode scale is not better than support percentiles at K = 2.
provenance: Fine-Tuning CLIP Models with Convolutional Features for Medical Anomaly Detection

B1-g0-C3.title: Prototype-radius normalisation of MVFA's few-shot branch
B1-g0-C3.summary: Cluster support patch features into normal prototypes per level, score test patches by distance to the nearest prototype divided by its radius, and fuse with the support-normalised zero-shot branch using MVFA's unchanged rule.
B1-g0-C3.research_idea: Independent variable: few-shot branch normalisation (test-set min-max; support percentiles; prototype-radius). Per level: k-means (k = min(32, number of support patches / 20)) on support patch features; radius r_k = 90th percentile of member distances; q = min_k ||f - P_k|| / r_k, mapped to [0, 1] by q / (1 + q). Dependent variables: image/pixel AUROC, sensitivity at 95% specificity, per-image score shift, memory and latency.
B1-g0-C3.hypothesis: Prototype-radius normalisation matches the percentile normaliser within 1 pixel-AUROC point at K >= 4 and outperforms it by at least 1 point at K = 2, while reducing the few-shot memory by at least 10x.
B1-g0-C3.rationale: The few-shot branch's raw score (1 - max cosine to the bank) has no intrinsic scale: what counts as far depends on how spread the normal patches are at that level. Spatial-FAD's prototypes suggest a scale: express each test patch's distance to its nearest normal prototype in units of that prototype's radius. The zero-shot branch is normalised with support percentiles as in the problem, and the 0.5 fusion and max pooling stay unchanged.
B1-g0-C3.method: 1) utils.py: fit_prototypes(support_feats_l, k) with torch k-means (20 iterations); radii. 2) test_few.py: few-shot map from q/(1+q) per level; zero-shot map with support percentiles; 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged; test-set min-max removed. 3) Report memory and latency. No training.
B1-g0-C3.experiment: Protocol: leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA checkpoints retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2, 4, 8, 16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws, mean and std; fusion weight 0.5 and max pooling unchanged in every variant. Baselines: the original transductive pipeline (test-set min-max) and the percentile normaliser of the problem statement (1st/99th percentiles of leave-one-out support patch scores). Motivating measurement for all variants: AUROC spread of the transductive pipeline over random half-size test subsets and at 10% and 50% prevalence. Metrics: image/pixel AUROC, sensitivity at 95% specificity, score shift, memory, latency. Falsified if pixel AUROC drops by more than 1 point at K >= 4 relative to the percentile normaliser.
provenance: Bridging Vision Foundation Model Priors with CLIP for Spatial-aware Few-shot Anomaly Detection in Medical Images

B1-g0-C4.title: Two-anchor scaling with support normals and synthetic lesions
B1-g0-C4.summary: Normalise each MVFA branch between the median score of support-normal patches and the median score of synthetic lesions pasted into those supports, removing all test-set statistics.
B1-g0-C4.research_idea: Independent variable: normaliser (test-set min-max; support percentiles; two-anchor synthetic scaling). For branch b and level l: lo = median LOO support-normal patch score; hi = median patch score over pasted-lesion pixels in 20 synthetic variants per support (patches from other supports, Poisson-blended, 1-5% of the area); z = clip((s - lo)/(hi - lo), -1, 3), rescaled to [0, 1]. Dependent variables: image/pixel AUROC, sensitivity at 95% specificity, realised specificity, per-image score shift.
B1-g0-C4.hypothesis: Two-anchor synthetic scaling keeps image AUROC within 1 point of the transductive pipeline at K >= 4 and yields realised specificity closer to 95% than support percentiles, because the synthetic anchor fixes the relative scale of the two branches.
B1-g0-C4.rationale: Min-max normalisation needs a low and a high anchor; MVFA takes both from the test set, and support percentiles take both from normal data only, so the high anchor is just the tail of normal. Following Fed-LoRA, synthetic lesions pasted into the target's own supports give a genuine high anchor: support normals map to 0 and synthetic lesions to 1, keeping MVFA's two-anchor logic, its 0.5 fusion and max pooling.
B1-g0-C4.method: 1) synth.py: synth_lesion(img, other) with Poisson blending; masks recorded. 2) utils.py: anchors(model, supports) computes lo and hi per branch and level. 3) test_few.py: per-image normalisation, unchanged 0.5 fusion and max pooling; test-set min-max removed. Hyper-parameters: 20 variants per support, area 1-5%, clip [-1, 3]; no training.
B1-g0-C4.experiment: Protocol: leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA checkpoints retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2, 4, 8, 16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws, mean and std; fusion weight 0.5 and max pooling unchanged in every variant. Baselines: the original transductive pipeline (test-set min-max) and the percentile normaliser of the problem statement (1st/99th percentiles of leave-one-out support patch scores). Motivating measurement for all variants: AUROC spread of the transductive pipeline over random half-size test subsets and at 10% and 50% prevalence. Metrics: image/pixel AUROC, sensitivity at 95% specificity, realised specificity, score shift. Falsified if AUROC drops by more than 1 point or realised specificity is not closer to 95% than with support percentiles.
provenance: Fed-LoRA: Cross-Domain Generative Knowledge Feedback for Few-Shot Medical Anomaly Detection

B1-g0-C5.title: Position-wise support normalisation of MVFA's branches
B1-g0-C5.summary: Normalise each branch's patch score by the leave-one-out support scores at the same grid position, shrunk towards the global support statistic, so anatomy-driven offsets are removed without test-set statistics.
B1-g0-C5.research_idea: Independent variable: normaliser (test-set min-max; global support percentiles; position-wise support normalisation). For branch b, level l and position j: mu_j, sd_j from the K LOO support scores at j (and its 3x3 neighbourhood), shrunk: mu*_j = (n mu_j + 20 mu_g)/(n + 20), likewise sd; z = (s_j - mu*_j)/sd*_j, mapped by a logistic to [0, 1]. Dependent variables: image/pixel AUROC, false-positive rate in normal images per position (heat map), per-image score shift.
B1-g0-C5.hypothesis: On spatially aligned modalities (BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC, OCT17), position-wise normalisation improves pixel AUROC by at least 1 point over global support percentiles at K >= 4, and it is not worse than global percentiles on ChestXray and HIS by more than 0.5 points.
B1-g0-C5.rationale: Medical images of one modality are roughly aligned, and ADAN shows that much of an adapted CLIP map reflects anatomy. A single global normaliser per branch therefore mixes positions where normal anatomy scores high (e.g., skull, retinal layers) with positions where it scores low. Normalising each grid position by the support-normal scores at that position (shrunk towards the global statistic because K is small) removes anatomy-driven offsets inductively, before the unchanged 0.5 fusion and max pooling.
B1-g0-C5.method: 1) utils.py: positional_refs(support_maps) computes per-position LOO statistics with a 3x3 neighbourhood and shrinkage weight 20. 2) test_few.py: per-image positional z-scores per branch and level, logistic map, 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged; test-set min-max removed. Hyper-parameters: neighbourhood 3x3, shrinkage 20 (ablation {5, 20, 80}); no training.
B1-g0-C5.experiment: Protocol: leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA checkpoints retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2, 4, 8, 16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws, mean and std; fusion weight 0.5 and max pooling unchanged in every variant. Baselines: the original transductive pipeline (test-set min-max) and the percentile normaliser of the problem statement (1st/99th percentiles of leave-one-out support patch scores). Motivating measurement for all variants: AUROC spread of the transductive pipeline over random half-size test subsets and at 10% and 50% prevalence. Metrics: image/pixel AUROC, positional false-positive maps, score shift. Ablations: shrinkage; neighbourhood size. Falsified if no pixel-AUROC gain on aligned modalities.
provenance: Anatomic-Decoupling Adaptation: A Unified Framework for Zero/Few-Shot Medical Anomaly Detection

B1-g0-C6.title: Anchor-geometry normalisation of MVFA's zero-shot branch
B1-g0-C6.summary: Replace the softmax output of the zero-shot branch by the patch projection on the unit anchor-difference direction, standardise both branches with support LOO statistics, and fuse them with MVFA's unchanged rule.
B1-g0-C6.research_idea: Independent variable: zero-shot branch representation and normaliser (test-set min-max on softmax; support percentiles on softmax; support standardisation of the unit-direction projection). For level l: u_l = (T_abn - T_nor)/||T_abn - T_nor||; zero-shot score s = <f_j/||f_j||, u_l>; z = (s - median_supp)/MAD_supp; few-shot branch standardised the same way; both mapped by a logistic to [0, 1]. Dependent variables: image/pixel AUROC, sensitivity at 95% specificity, and stability of the operating threshold across held-out modalities.
B1-g0-C6.hypothesis: Standardising the unit-direction projection makes the support-derived threshold transfer across held-out modalities with a realised-specificity spread at least 5 points smaller than with percentile-normalised softmax scores, at equal AUROC (within 1 point).
B1-g0-C6.rationale: MVFA's zero-shot branch is a two-way softmax over text anchors, so by Do Words Matter? its scale is fixed by the length of the anchor difference times the feature norm, a quantity that is constant per level and known without any test image. The two branches can then be put on a common scale analytically: express the zero-shot branch as the projection on the unit anchor-difference direction, and standardise it and the few-shot branch with support LOO statistics on that projection. This replaces test-set min-max with a geometry-derived, inductive normaliser and keeps 0.5 fusion and max pooling.
B1-g0-C6.method: 1) utils.py: anchor_direction(text_features) per level. 2) test_few.py: zero-shot map = projection on u_l; support LOO median and MAD per branch and level; logistic map; 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged; test-set min-max removed. Hyper-parameters: none; no training.
B1-g0-C6.experiment: Protocol: leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA checkpoints retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2, 4, 8, 16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws, mean and std; fusion weight 0.5 and max pooling unchanged in every variant. Baselines: the original transductive pipeline (test-set min-max) and the percentile normaliser of the problem statement (1st/99th percentiles of leave-one-out support patch scores). Motivating measurement for all variants: AUROC spread of the transductive pipeline over random half-size test subsets and at 10% and 50% prevalence. Metrics: image/pixel AUROC, sensitivity at 95% specificity, spread of realised specificity across held-out datasets. Falsified if the threshold spread is not reduced.
provenance: Do Words Matter? What Text Contributes to Few and Full-Shot Vision-Language Anomaly Detection

B1-g1-o1.title: Position-wise low anchor and synthetic high anchor for inductive MVFA scoring
B1-g1-o1.summary: Normalise each branch per grid position between a shrunk position-wise median of leave-one-out support scores (low anchor) and the median score of synthetic lesions pasted into the supports (high anchor), keeping MVFA's 0.5 fusion and max pooling.
B1-g1-o1.hypothesis: On spatially aligned held-out modalities, the position-wise/synthetic two-anchor normaliser keeps image and pixel AUROC within 1 point of the transductive pipeline at K >= 4 and improves pixel AUROC by at least 1 point over global support percentiles.
B1-g1-o1.rationale: The position-wise parent removes anatomy-driven offsets but has no principled upper scale; the synthetic-anchor parent gives an upper scale but treats all positions alike. Using the position-wise statistic as the low anchor and the synthetic lesion score as a global high anchor gives a normaliser that is both anatomy-aware and on a common scale across branches, without any test-set statistic.
B1-g1-o1.method: 1) utils.py: positional_low(support_maps): per-position LOO medians with 3x3 neighbourhood and shrinkage 20 towards the global median; synthetic_high(model, supports): 20 Poisson-blended lesions per support (1-5% area), median lesion-pixel score per branch and level. 2) test_few.py: z = clip((s_j - lo_j)/(hi - lo_j), -1, 3) rescaled to [0, 1]; 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged; test-set min-max removed. No training.
B1-g1-o1.experiment: Leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2, 4, 8, 16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws; 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged. Baselines: transductive MVFA pipeline, support percentiles (problem statement). Additional baselines: position-wise only; synthetic two-anchor only. Metrics: image/pixel AUROC, sensitivity at 95% specificity, per-position false-positive maps. Falsified if no gain over global percentiles on aligned modalities.
provenance: Anatomic-Decoupling Adaptation: A Unified Framework for Zero/Few-Shot Medical Anomaly Detection
Fed-LoRA: Cross-Domain Generative Knowledge Feedback for Few-Shot Medical Anomaly Detection

B1-g1-o2.title: Position-wise leave-one-out empirical CDF with neighbourhood pooling
B1-g1-o2.summary: Map each patch score through the empirical CDF of leave-one-out support scores from the same grid neighbourhood, mixed with the global support CDF according to how many reference values the neighbourhood holds.
B1-g1-o2.hypothesis: At K >= 4 on spatially aligned held-out modalities, the position-wise empirical CDF improves pixel AUROC by at least 1 point over the global empirical CDF and keeps image AUROC within 1 point of the transductive pipeline, while every score stays exactly invariant to the test set.
B1-g1-o2.rationale: The empirical-CDF parent gives an assumption-free, test-set-invariant scale but ignores anatomy; the position-wise parent removes anatomy offsets but relies on mean/standard-deviation statistics from very few values. Their combination keeps the rank-based CDF and makes the reference set local: for position j the references are all LOO support patch scores within a 3x3 (level 4: 5x5) neighbourhood, and the local CDF is mixed with the global one with weight n_j/(n_j + 50).
B1-g1-o2.method: 1) utils.py: build_local_refs(support_maps, radius): sorted arrays per position; global array as in the parent. 2) cdf_mix(s, R_local, R_global) = w F_local(s) + (1 - w) F_global(s), w = n/(n + 50). 3) test_few.py: apply per branch and level, then 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged; test-set min-max removed. Hyper-parameters: radius {1, 2}, mixing constant {10, 50, 200}. No training.
B1-g1-o2.experiment: Leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2, 4, 8, 16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws; 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged. Baselines: transductive MVFA pipeline, support percentiles (problem statement). Additional baseline: global empirical CDF. Metrics: image/pixel AUROC, sensitivity at 95% specificity. Falsified if the local CDF is not better than the global CDF in pixel AUROC on aligned modalities.
provenance: MadCLIP: Few-shot Medical Anomaly Detection with CLIP
Beyond Static Anchors: Bounded Prototype Conditioning for Language-Free Medical Anomaly Detection
Anatomic-Decoupling Adaptation: A Unified Framework for Zero/Few-Shot Medical Anomaly Detection

B1-g1-o3.title: Empirical CDF of anatomy residuals for inductive MVFA scoring
B1-g1-o3.summary: Subtract a shrunk position-wise median of support scores from every patch score and map the residual through one global leave-one-out empirical CDF of support residuals, then fuse with MVFA's unchanged rule.
B1-g1-o3.hypothesis: Mapping position-wise residuals through a global empirical CDF matches the global empirical CDF in image AUROC (within 1 point) and improves pixel AUROC by at least 1 point on aligned modalities, with lower variance across support draws at K = 2 than the position-wise CDF.
B1-g1-o3.rationale: This combination takes the positional part from the position-wise parent only as a location correction, and the scale from the empirical-CDF parent as a single global reference. Separating location (local, needs few values) from scale (global, needs many) avoids estimating local spreads from a handful of supports, which is the weak point of both a position-wise z-score and a local CDF at K = 2.
B1-g1-o3.method: 1) utils.py: positional_median(support_maps) with 3x3 neighbourhood and shrinkage 20; residual reference set R = {s - med_j} over all LOO support patches. 2) test_few.py: r = s_j - med_j; F(r) via searchsorted on R; 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged; test-set min-max removed. No training.
B1-g1-o3.experiment: Leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2, 4, 8, 16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws; 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged. Baselines: transductive MVFA pipeline, support percentiles (problem statement). Additional baselines: global empirical CDF; position-wise CDF. Metric of stability: standard deviation of AUROC over support draws. Falsified if residual CDF is not more stable than the position-wise CDF at K = 2.
provenance: MadCLIP: Few-shot Medical Anomaly Detection with CLIP
Beyond Static Anchors: Bounded Prototype Conditioning for Language-Free Medical Anomaly Detection
Anatomic-Decoupling Adaptation: A Unified Framework for Zero/Few-Shot Medical Anomaly Detection

B1-g1-o4.title: Matched-support normalisation: normalise each test image against its most similar supports
B1-g1-o4.summary: Instead of per-position statistics (which assume alignment) or a global analytic scale, normalise each test image's branch scores with the leave-one-out scores of the m supports whose global CLIP embedding is closest to it.
B1-g1-o4.hypothesis: Normalising with the m = min(3, K) nearest supports improves pixel AUROC by at least 1 point over global support percentiles at K >= 8 on all six held-out datasets, including the unaligned ChestXray and HIS where position-wise normalisation does not apply.
B1-g1-o4.rationale: The position-wise parent captures that normal score levels vary with anatomy, but assumes images are aligned; the anchor-geometry parent shows that a branch's scale is set by global properties of the representation. A different mechanism follows: anatomy and acquisition vary per image, and the supports that look most like a test image carry the most relevant normal score distribution. Choosing the reference per test image by global embedding similarity handles variation without spatial alignment and stays inductive, since it uses only the supports.
B1-g1-o4.method: 1) utils.py: support_cls(supports): CLS embeddings of the supports (frozen CLIP). 2) test_few.py: for a test image, cosine similarity of its CLS to the supports; select top m; reference set = their LOO patch scores per branch and level; normalise with 1st/99th percentiles of that set; 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged; test-set min-max removed. 3) Hyper-parameters: m in {1, 3, 5}. No training.
B1-g1-o4.experiment: Leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2, 4, 8, 16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws; 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged. Baselines: transductive MVFA pipeline, support percentiles (problem statement). Additional baseline: position-wise normalisation. Metrics: image/pixel AUROC, sensitivity at 95% specificity. Falsified if no gain over global percentiles at K >= 8.
provenance: Anatomic-Decoupling Adaptation: A Unified Framework for Zero/Few-Shot Medical Anomaly Detection
Do Words Matter? What Text Contributes to Few and Full-Shot Vision-Language Anomaly Detection

B1-g1-o5.title: Split-conformal image thresholds from support leave-one-out maxima
B1-g1-o5.summary: Treat the K normal supports as a calibration set: normalise branches by leave-one-out support statistics, compute each support's leave-one-out image score (max of the fused map), and set the operating threshold as a conformal quantile, which bounds the false-positive rate on new normal images by construction.
B1-g1-o5.hypothesis: With the threshold at the ceil((K+1)(1 - alpha))-th smallest support leave-one-out image score, the realised false-positive rate on held-out normal test images stays at or below alpha + 1/(K+1) on every BMAD dataset where test normals are exchangeable with the supports, while transductive min-max thresholds give realised false-positive rates that vary by more than 15 points across datasets.
B1-g1-o5.rationale: The anchor-geometry parent seeks a scale that makes thresholds transfer; an analogous principle from distribution-free inference gives a guarantee instead of a hope. If support normals and test normals are exchangeable, the rank of a new normal image's score among the K leave-one-out support scores is uniform, so a conformal quantile controls the false-positive rate at any K without modelling the score distribution. This needs exactly what the problem's inductive normaliser provides — per-image scores computed from supports only — and it turns MVFA's threshold-free AUROC evaluation into a deployable decision rule with a stated error bound; where the bound is violated, it measures non-exchangeability (support/test shift) directly.
B1-g1-o5.method: 1) test_few.py: inductive normalisation by support percentiles (problem statement); 0.5 fusion; image score = max of fused map. 2) For i in 1..K: score support i with the bank and statistics of the other K-1 supports -> s_i. 3) tau_alpha = sorted(s)[ceil((K+1)(1 - alpha)) - 1] (if the index exceeds K, report 'no valid threshold' for that alpha and K). 4) Report realised FPR on test normals and sensitivity on test abnormals at alpha in {0.1, 0.2}. No training.
B1-g1-o5.experiment: Leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2, 4, 8, 16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws; 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged. Baselines: transductive MVFA pipeline, support percentiles (problem statement). Metrics: realised FPR vs. the bound alpha + 1/(K+1), sensitivity, AUROC (unchanged by thresholding), fraction of (K, alpha) cells with a valid threshold. Falsified if realised FPR exceeds the bound on datasets whose test normals come from the same source as the supports.
provenance: Do Words Matter? What Text Contributes to Few and Full-Shot Vision-Language Anomaly Detection
MadCLIP: Few-shot Medical Anomaly Detection with CLIP
Beyond Static Anchors: Bounded Prototype Conditioning for Language-Free Medical Anomaly Detection

B1-g1-o6.title: Analytic zero-shot scale plus support CDF for the few-shot branch
B1-g1-o6.summary: Normalise MVFA's zero-shot branch without any target data, from the anchor geometry and source-validation statistics, and only the few-shot branch from the K supports via a leave-one-out empirical CDF.
B1-g1-o6.hypothesis: With the zero-shot branch normalised analytically and the few-shot branch by the support CDF, fused image AUROC stays within 1 point of the transductive pipeline at K >= 4, and at K = 2 it loses at least 1 point less than normalising both branches from the supports.
B1-g1-o6.rationale: The anchor-geometry parent shows that the zero-shot branch reads the anchors only through their difference, so its scale is a property of the trained model, not of the target. The CDF parent gives a robust support-based scale where target data are needed. A different allocation follows: the zero-shot branch needs no target statistics at all (its normaliser can be fixed on source validation), and the scarce K supports are spent only on the memory-bank branch, whose scale genuinely depends on the target. This halves the number of quantities estimated from K images.
B1-g1-o6.method: 1) calibrate_zero.py: on source validation splits, compute zero-shot patch projections on the unit anchor-difference direction per level; store median and MAD of normal patches. 2) test_few.py: zero-shot z = (proj - median_src)/MAD_src mapped by a logistic; few-shot via LOO empirical CDF of support scores; 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged; test-set min-max removed. No adapter training.

Baselines: transductive MVFA pipeline, support percentiles (problem statement). Additional baselines: both branches by support CDF; both by support percentiles. B1-g2-o1.title: Alignment-adaptive residual CDF: weighting the positional correction by measured anatomy alignment
B1-g2-o1.summary: Use the residual empirical CDF (positional median subtracted, global CDF of residuals) but weight the positional correction by how much the supports' normal scores actually vary with position, so unaligned modalities fall back to the plain global CDF automatically.
B1-g2-o1.hypothesis: The alignment-adaptive residual CDF is never worse than the global empirical CDF by more than 0.3 pixel-AUROC points on any held-out dataset, and on spatially aligned datasets it keeps at least 80% of the full residual-CDF gain, at all K.
B1-g2-o1.rationale: The global-CDF parent is safe but ignores anatomy; the residual-CDF parent removes anatomy offsets but assumes alignment. Their combination measures alignment from the supports themselves: the share of variance of leave-one-out support scores explained by grid position (an intraclass correlation, rho). The positional correction is applied with weight rho, so a modality whose normal score level does not depend on position (ChestXray crops, histopathology tiles) receives the plain global CDF and a well-aligned one receives the residual CDF.
B1-g2-o1.method: 1) utils.py: rho = var_between_positions / (var_between + var_within) of LOO support scores per branch and level (positions pooled in 3x3 neighbourhoods). 2) Residual r = s_j - rho x med_j (med_j shrunk positional median); reference set built from support LOO residuals computed the same way. 3) test_few.py: F(r) via searchsorted; 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged; test-set min-max removed. No training.
B1-g2-o1.experiment: Leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2, 4, 8, 16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws; 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged. Baselines: transductive MVFA pipeline, support percentiles (problem statement). Additional baselines: global empirical CDF; residual CDF with rho = 1. Report rho per dataset. Falsified if the adaptive variant is worse than the global CDF by more than 0.3 points on any dataset.

B1-g2-o2.title: Feature-registered positional references
B1-g2-o2.summary: Before computing positional statistics, align each support's patch grid to the test image by a small rigid shift found by maximising CLIP patch-feature correlation, so the positional correction of the residual CDF works even where images are only roughly aligned.
B1-g2-o2.hypothesis: Registering supports to the test image by integer patch shifts (up to +-3 patches) increases the pixel-AUROC gain of the residual CDF over the global CDF by at least 50% on BrainMRI, LiverCT and RESC, at less than 10% additional inference time.
B1-g2-o2.rationale: The residual-CDF parent assumes that grid position j means the same anatomy in every image. In BMAD this holds only roughly: brains, livers and retinas are shifted between slices and scans. Instead of giving up positional information on such data, a cheap rigid registration in feature space — choose the integer shift that maximises correlation of frozen CLIP patch features between support and test — restores the correspondence. The method stays inductive, as it uses only the test image and the supports.
B1-g2-o2.method: 1) utils.py: register(F_test, F_supp, max_shift=3): for all shifts in [-3, 3]^2 compute mean cosine of overlapping patch features (level 2); return best shift. 2) Positional median per test image computed from shifted support maps (LOO for supports). 3) Residual CDF as in the parent; 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged; test-set min-max removed. No training.

B1-g2-o3.title: Augmented-support reference sets for inductive normalisation at small K
B1-g2-o3.summary: Enlarge the leave-one-out reference set of every normaliser by scoring label-preserving augmentations of the K normal supports (flips, small shifts and rotations, mild intensity jitter), so the reference distribution reflects normal variability even at K = 2.
B1-g2-o3.hypothesis: At K = 2, building the empirical-CDF reference from 16 augmentations per support reduces the standard deviation of image AUROC across support draws by at least 30% and increases mean pixel AUROC by at least 1 point over the unaugmented reference, with no benefit expected at K = 16.
B1-g2-o3.rationale: Both parents spend all their effort on how to map scores, while their common weakness is how few normal scores are available: at K = 2 the reference consists of two images scored against a one-image bank. A different lever is the reference itself. Normal anatomy varies by position, orientation and intensity; label-preserving augmentations of the supports sample this variation and give many more leave-one-out reference scores without any extra data. Augmented views are scored against the bank of the other supports only, so the scheme stays strictly inductive.
B1-g2-o3.method: 1) utils.py: augment(x, n=16): horizontal flip (where anatomically valid), shifts up to 8 px, rotations up to 10 degrees, gamma in [0.8, 1.2]. 2) build_refs: for each support i and each augmented view, few-shot scores against the bank of the other supports (unaugmented) and zero-shot scores; pool into the reference arrays. 3) test_few.py: empirical CDF per branch and level; 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged; test-set min-max removed. Hyper-parameters: n in {4, 16, 64}. No training.
B1-g2-o3.experiment: Leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2, 4, 8, 16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws; 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged. B1-g2-o4.title: Extreme-value tail extension of the support CDF
B1-g2-o4.summary: Model the upper tail of each branch's leave-one-out support scores with a generalised Pareto distribution, so scores beyond the largest support value are still ordered instead of all mapping to 1, which matters because the image score is the maximum of the fused map.
B1-g2-o4.hypothesis: Replacing the saturated top of the empirical CDF with a generalised-Pareto tail fitted above the 90th support percentile increases image AUROC by at least 1 point over the plain empirical CDF at K <= 4, where the fraction of test images whose max fused score is tied at the ceiling exceeds 20%.
B1-g2-o4.rationale: An empirical CDF is flat at 1 above the largest reference value. With few supports, many test patches — in normal and abnormal images alike — exceed every support score, so after max pooling a large share of test images obtain the same ceiling score and AUROC loses resolution exactly where it matters. Extreme value theory gives a principled extrapolation: exceedances over a high threshold follow a generalised Pareto distribution, whose parameters can be fitted from the support scores above their 90th percentile (thousands of patches even at K = 2). The resulting CDF is strictly increasing in the tail and remains test-set invariant.
B1-g2-o4.method: 1) utils.py: fit_gpd(R, q=0.9) by maximum likelihood (scipy.stats.genpareto) per branch and level. 2) F(s) = ECDF(s) for s <= u; F(s) = 0.9 + 0.1 x GPD_cdf(s - u) above the threshold u. 3) test_few.py: apply per branch and level; 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged; test-set min-max removed. 4) Report the fraction of tied image scores. No training.
B1-g2-o4.experiment: Leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2, 4, 8, 16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws; 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged. Baselines: transductive MVFA pipeline, support percentiles (problem statement). Additional baseline: plain LOO empirical CDF. Metrics: AUROC, fraction of tied image scores. B1-g2-o5.title: Self-referenced residuals: removing each image's own score offset before support-CDF mapping
B1-g2-o5.summary: Subtract from every patch score the median of the same image's own patch scores (a per-image offset reflecting acquisition and intensity) and map the residual through the leave-one-out support CDF of residuals computed the same way, which stays strictly inductive because it uses only the image itself and the supports.
B1-g2-o5.hypothesis: Self-referenced residual normalisation improves image AUROC by at least 1.5 points over the exact leave-one-out residual CDF on held-out datasets with strong acquisition variation (ChestXray, HIS, OCT17), and changes it by less than 0.5 points on the others.
B1-g2-o5.rationale: The residual-CDF parents remove offsets that depend on position, but much of the variation in medical scores is per image: scanner, intensity window, stain, patient size. An image's own median patch score measures this offset without any other test image, because most of every image — even an abnormal one — is normal tissue. Subtracting it before mapping through a reference built the same way from supports removes per-image offsets inductively; diffuse lesions that shift the median are the risk, which the per-dataset evaluation measures.
B1-g2-o5.method: 1) test_few.py: for every image (supports and tests) and each branch and level: r_j = s_j - median(s); for supports use leave-one-out bank scores. 2) Reference R = pooled support residuals; F(r) by searchsorted. 3) 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged; test-set min-max removed. 4) Ablation: positional + self-referenced residual. No training.

Baselines: transductive MVFA pipeline, support percentiles (problem statement). Additional baselines: exact LOO residual CDF; global CDF. Diagnostic: correlation of per-image median score with image AUROC loss. Falsified if no gain on ChestXray, HIS or OCT17.

B1-g2-o6.title: Similarity-weighted conformal thresholds on residual-CDF scores
B1-g2-o6.summary: Keep residual-CDF scoring but replace the plain split-conformal quantile with a weighted conformal quantile in which supports similar to the test image (CLIP CLS similarity) count more, so the threshold adapts to each image while keeping an approximate false-positive bound under covariate shift.
B1-g2-o6.hypothesis: Similarity-weighted conformal thresholds reduce the spread of realised false-positive rates across held-out datasets by at least 5 points relative to unweighted conformal thresholds at K >= 8, while keeping the mean realised false-positive rate within 2 points of alpha.
B1-g2-o6.rationale: The parent's split-conformal step assumes that test normals are exchangeable with the supports; across BMAD datasets this fails when a test image comes from a different part of the anatomy or another scanner than most supports. Weighted conformal prediction (Tibshirani et al., 2019) keeps an approximate guarantee under covariate shift by weighting calibration points with a likelihood ratio, which can be approximated by similarity of global features. The substitute targets the same quantity (a per-image threshold with controlled false positives) with the same evaluation.
B1-g2-o6.method: 1) Residual-CDF scoring as in the parent (exact LOO). 2) For test image x: weights w_i = exp(cos(cls_x, cls_i)/tau) over supports, plus w_{K+1} for the test point; tau from source validation. 3) Threshold = weighted (1 - alpha) quantile of support LOO image scores with the test point's mass at +infinity. 4) Report realised FPR and sensitivity at alpha in {0.1, 0.2}. No training.

B1-g3-o1.title: Meta-selected normaliser from simulated source episodes
B1-g3-o1.summary: Simulate few-shot episodes on the source modalities, record which inductive normaliser (global CDF, residual CDF, alignment-adaptive residual CDF) works best as a function of support-measurable features (alignment rho, K, score spread), and use this rule to pick the normaliser for the unseen modality from its supports alone.
B1-g3-o1.hypothesis: The meta-selected normaliser is within 0.3 AUROC points of the best normaliser in hindsight on at least five of six held-out datasets, and on average better than any single fixed normaliser.
B1-g3-o1.rationale: The alignment-adaptive parent blends two normalisers with one statistic. A more general principle — algorithm selection by meta-learning — chooses among several normalisers using features that can be measured on the K supports. The source modalities provide labelled episodes on which the choice can be learned, and leave-one-modality-out evaluation tests whether that choice transfers.
B1-g3-o1.method: 1) meta_select.py: on each source modality's validation split, 50 episodes per K; features: rho, K, coefficient of variation of LOO support scores, fraction of foreground patches; label: best normaliser by episode AUROC. 2) Fit a depth-2 decision tree on the pooled episodes of the training fold. 3) Target: compute features from the supports, choose the normaliser; 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged; test-set min-max removed. No adapter training.

B1-g3-o2.title: Foreground-size-aware Gumbel normalisation of the max-pooled image score
B1-g3-o2.summary: Because the maximum of N normal patch scores grows with N, normalise each image's max fused score by a Gumbel distribution of leave-one-out support maxima whose location is adjusted for the image's number of foreground patches, so large-anatomy images are not systematically scored as more anomalous.
B1-g3-o2.hypothesis: Adjusting the max-pooled image score for foreground size with a support-fitted Gumbel model increases image AUROC by at least 1 point on held-out datasets whose foreground area varies strongly between images (LiverCT, ChestXray), and changes it by less than 0.5 points elsewhere.
B1-g3-o2.rationale: The EVT parent extends the patch-level CDF tail, but the image score is the maximum over all patches, and a maximum of more patches is larger even if every patch is normal. In BMAD the foreground area differs strongly between slices and images, so with max pooling fixed by the problem, images with more tissue get higher scores for no pathological reason. Block-maxima theory says that the maximum of N i.i.d. normal scores is approximately Gumbel with location increasing in log N. Fitting this relation on the supports (leave-one-out maxima of support images and of their random sub-regions of different sizes) gives an inductive, size-aware normaliser of the image score.
B1-g3-o2.method: 1) Foreground mask per image by Otsu on intensity (patch-level). 2) For each support i (LOO): maxima of the fused normalised map over random sub-regions of sizes N in {25%, 50%, 100%} of its foreground; fit Gumbel location mu(N) = a + b log N and scale beta by maximum likelihood. 3) Test image: z = (max - mu(N_fg)) / beta, image score = Gumbel CDF(z). 4) Pixel maps unchanged; patch normaliser = support percentiles (problem statement). No training.
B1-g3-o2.experiment: Leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2, 4, 8, 16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws; 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged. Baselines: transductive MVFA pipeline, support percentiles (problem statement). Additional baseline: support-percentile normaliser without size correction. Diagnostic: correlation of image score with foreground size among normal test images before and after correction. Falsified if no AUROC gain on LiverCT and ChestXray.

B1-g3-o3.title: Optimal-transport correspondence for patch-wise normal references
B1-g3-o3.summary: Instead of grid positions or rigid shifts, match every test patch to support patches by entropic optimal transport over feature and position costs, and normalise its score against the leave-one-out scores of the support patches it is matched to.
B1-g3-o3.hypothesis: Optimal-transport-matched references improve pixel AUROC by at least 1 point over the alignment-adaptive residual CDF on BrainMRI, LiverCT and RESC, and by at least 0.5 points on the unaligned datasets, at less than 2x inference time.
B1-g3-o3.rationale: Alignment-adaptive correction decides how much positional correspondence to trust but cannot repair it. Optimal transport, used for patch-prompt alignment in recent medical anomaly detection, gives a soft correspondence between two sets of patches that respects both appearance and position, and works on deformed or partially aligned anatomy. The scores of the matched support patches then form a reference that is specific to the anatomy of each test patch.
B1-g3-o3.method: 1) For a test image and each support: cost C_ij = (1 - cos(f_i, f_j)) + 0.1 ||pos_i - pos_j||; Sinkhorn with entropy 0.05, 50 iterations (level 2 features). 2) Matched reference of test patch i: transport-weighted LOO scores of support patches; normalised score = weighted rank of s_i within them; mix with the global CDF (weight 0.2). 3) 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged; test-set min-max removed. No training.

B1-g3-o4.title: Content-conditioned expected-normal-score regression
B1-g3-o4.summary: Train on the source modalities a small regressor that predicts the expected normal anomaly score of a patch from its frozen CLIP feature, and normalise target scores by the residual from this prediction (re-centred with the supports), removing anatomy-driven offsets without assuming spatial alignment.
B1-g3-o4.hypothesis: Content-conditioned residual normalisation improves pixel AUROC by at least 1 point over global support percentiles on all six held-out datasets, including the unaligned ChestXray and HIS where positional residuals do not apply.
B1-g3-o4.rationale: The residual parent removes anatomy offsets by grid position, which only works where images are aligned. The underlying cause is that some normal tissue types score systematically higher; this is a property of the patch's content, not of its position. A regressor from frozen CLIP features to the score of normal patches, trained on the source modalities' normal images, predicts this offset for any patch, and the residual is then mapped through the support CDF. Because the regressor is trained on sources only and re-centred with the target supports, the method stays inductive and leave-one-modality-out.
B1-g3-o4.method: 1) train_offset.py (per fold): on normal source training images, collect (frozen level-l patch feature, branch score) pairs; fit a 2-layer MLP (768-128-1) per branch and level with MSE, 5 epochs. 2) Target: r = s - g(f) - c, where c is the median residual of the supports (LOO). 3) F(r) via the LOO support CDF of residuals; 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged; test-set min-max removed. Hyper-parameters: hidden size 128; ablation with a linear regressor.

B1-g3-o5.title: Exact leave-one-out, alignment-adaptive residual CDF
B1-g3-o5.summary: Combine the alignment-adaptive residual CDF (positional correction weighted by measured alignment) with a strictly leave-one-out construction of the support residual references, so the method is safe on unaligned modalities and unbiased at small K.
B1-g3-o5.hypothesis: The exact leave-one-out alignment-adaptive residual CDF matches the alignment-adaptive residual CDF in AUROC (within 0.5 points) and reduces the gap between nominal and realised specificity at the support-derived 95% threshold by at least 3 points at K <= 4.
B1-g3-o5.rationale: The alignment-adaptive parent decides how much positional correction to apply; the residual parent's weak point at small K is that a support's residual reference uses a positional median that includes the support itself, which makes support residuals too small and thresholds too low. Building every support's residuals with the median, alignment estimate and memory bank of the other K-1 supports removes that bias while keeping the adaptive safety of the first parent.
B1-g3-o5.method: 1) For i in 1..K: from the other K-1 supports compute bank_{-i}, positional median med_{-i}, alignment rho_{-i}; residuals of support i: s_ij - rho_{-i} med_{-i,j}; pool into R. 2) Test image: med and rho from all K supports; r = s_j - rho med_j; F(r) by searchsorted on R. 3) 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged; test-set min-max removed. No training.

B1-g3-o6.title: Multi-scale positional residuals
B1-g3-o6.summary: Subtract positional medians computed at several grid resolutions (full grid, 2x2-pooled, 4x4-pooled) and map the combined residual through one leave-one-out support CDF, so coarse anatomy offsets and fine structure offsets are removed without estimating each from a few values.
B1-g3-o6.hypothesis: Multi-scale positional residuals improve pixel AUROC by at least 0.5 points over the single-scale residual CDF on aligned held-out datasets at K <= 4, with smaller variance across support draws.
B1-g3-o6.rationale: The single-scale residual estimates one median per grid position, which at K = 2 is noisy. Multi-resolution decompositions (as in image pyramids and wavelets) estimate coarse components from many values and fine components from few, and combine them with shrinkage. Applying this to positional normal offsets gives a better bias-variance trade-off at small K while keeping the method inductive.
B1-g3-o6.method: 1) For each branch and level: medians at pooling factors {1, 2, 4} from LOO support maps; combined offset o_j = sum_s w_s med_s(j) with w_s proportional to the number of values per cell (shrinkage). 2) r = s_j - o_j; F(r) from the LOO support residual reference. 3) 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged; test-set min-max removed.
